        SUM(CASE WHEN match_runs >= 100 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS matches_100,
        SUM(balls_faced) AS total_balls_faced
    FROM batting_match
    GROUP BY player_id
),
dismissal_summary AS (
    SELECT
        player_out AS player_id,
        COUNT(*) AS total_dismissals
    FROM wicket_taken
    WHERE player_out IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY player_out
),
bowling_match AS (
    SELECT
        bb.match_id,
        bb.bowler AS player_id,
        SUM(COALESCE(bs.runs_scored, 0)) AS runs_given,
        COUNT(*) AS balls_bowled,
        SUM(
            CASE
                WHEN wt.player_out IS NOT NULL
                 AND LOWER(TRIM(COALESCE(wt.kind_out, ''))) NOT IN (
                     'run out',
                     'retired hurt',
                     'retired out',
                     'obstructing the field',
                     'timed out',
                     'handled the ball',
                     'hit the ball twice'
                 )
                THEN 1
                ELSE 0
            END
        ) AS wickets_taken
    FROM ball_by_ball AS bb
    LEFT JOIN batsman_scored AS bs
        ON bs.match_id = bb.match_id
       AND bs.over_id = bb.over_id
       AND bs.ball_id = bb.ball_id
       AND bs.innings_no = bb.innings_no
    LEFT JOIN wicket_taken AS wt
        ON wt.match_id = bb.match_id
       AND wt.over_id = bb.over_id
       AND wt.ball_id = bb.ball_id
       AND wt.innings_no = bb.innings_no
    GROUP BY bb.match_id, bb.bowler
),
bowling_summary AS (
    SELECT
        player_id,
        SUM(wickets_taken) AS total_wickets,
        SUM(runs_given) AS total_runs_given,
        SUM(balls_bowled) AS total_balls_bowled
    FROM bowling_match
    GROUP BY player_id
),
ranked_bowling AS (
    SELECT
        player_id,
        match_id,
        wickets_taken,
        runs_given,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY player_id
            ORDER BY wickets_taken DESC, runs_given ASC, match_id
        ) AS rn
    FROM bowling_match
),
best_bowling AS (
    SELECT
        player_id,
        wickets_taken,
        runs_given
    FROM ranked_bowling
    WHERE rn = 1
)
SELECT
    p.player_id,
    p.player_name,
    rr.role,
    p.batting_hand,
    p.bowling_skill,
    COALESCE(bs.total_runs, 0) AS total_runs_scored,
    COALESCE(mc.total_matches, 0) AS total_matches_played,
    COALESCE(ds.total_dismissals, 0) AS total_times_dismissed,
    (1.0 * COALESCE(bs.total_runs, 0))
        / NULLIF(COALESCE(ds.total_dismissals, 0), 0) AS batting_average,
    COALESCE(bs.highest_score, 0) AS highest_score,
    COALESCE(bs.matches_30, 0) AS matches_scored_at_least_30,
    COALESCE(bs.matches_50, 0) AS matches_scored_at_least_50,
    COALESCE(bs.matches_100, 0) AS matches_scored_at_least_100,
    COALESCE(bs.total_balls_faced, 0) AS total_balls_faced,
    (100.0 * COALESCE(bs.total_runs, 0))
        / NULLIF(COALESCE(bs.total_balls_faced, 0), 0) AS strike_rate,
    COALESCE(bws.total_wickets, 0) AS total_wickets_taken,
    (6.0 * COALESCE(bws.total_runs_given, 0))
        / NULLIF(COALESCE(bws.total_balls_bowled, 0), 0) AS economy_rate,
    COALESCE(
        CAST(bb.wickets_taken AS TEXT) || '-' || CAST(bb.runs_given AS TEXT),
        '0-0'
    ) AS best_bowling_performance
FROM player AS p
LEFT JOIN ranked_roles AS rr
    ON rr.player_id = p.player_id
   AND rr.rn = 1
LEFT JOIN match_counts AS mc
    ON mc.player_id = p.player_id
LEFT JOIN batting_summary AS bs
    ON bs.player_id = p.player_id
LEFT JOIN dismissal_summary AS ds
    ON ds.player_id = p.player_id
LEFT JOIN bowling_summary AS bws
    ON bws.player_id = p.player_id
LEFT JOIN best_bowling AS bb
    ON bb.player_id = p.player_id
ORDER BY p.player_id

luna.question: Which problems exceed the total number of times they appear in the solution table when counting all occurrences, across steps 1, 2, and 3, where any non-"Stack" model's maximum test score is lower than the "Stack" model's test score for the same step and version?
luna.sql:
WITH model_max AS (
    SELECT
        name,
        version,
        step,
        model,
        MAX(test_score) AS max_test_score
    FROM model_score
    WHERE step IN (1, 2, 3)
    GROUP BY name, version, step, model
),
qualifying_counts AS (
    SELECT
        nonstack.name,
        COUNT(*) AS qualifying_count
    FROM model_max AS nonstack
    JOIN model_max AS stack
      ON stack.name = nonstack.name
     AND stack.version = nonstack.version
     AND stack.step = nonstack.step
     AND stack.model = 'Stack'
    WHERE nonstack.model <> 'Stack'
      AND nonstack.max_test_score < stack.max_test_score
    GROUP BY nonstack.name
),
solution_counts AS (
    SELECT name, COUNT(*) AS solution_count
    FROM solution
    GROUP BY name
)
SELECT p.name
FROM problem AS p
JOIN qualifying_counts AS q
  ON q.name = p.name
LEFT JOIN solution_counts AS s
  ON s.name = p.name
WHERE q.qualifying_count > COALESCE(s.solution_count, 0)
ORDER BY p.name

luna.question: Identify the L1_model associated with each model (specified by name and version) that occurs most frequently for each status ('strong' or 'soft'), along with the number of times it occurs. A model has a 'strong' status if, for any of its steps, the maximum test score among non-'Stack' models is less than the 'Stack' model's test score. It has a 'soft' status if the maximum test score among non-'Stack' models equals the 'Stack' model's test score. Count how many times each L1_model is associated with a 'strong' or 'soft' status across all models, and determine which L1_model has the highest occurrence for each status.
luna.sql:
WITH step_scores AS (
    SELECT
        name,
        version,
        step,
        MAX(CASE WHEN model = 'Stack' THEN test_score END) AS stack_score,
        MAX(CASE WHEN model <> 'Stack' THEN test_score END) AS non_stack_score
    FROM model_score
    GROUP BY name, version, step
),
status_models AS (
    SELECT name, version, 'strong' AS status
    FROM step_scores
    WHERE non_stack_score < stack_score
    GROUP BY name, version
    UNION
    SELECT name, version, 'soft' AS status
    FROM step_scores
    WHERE non_stack_score = stack_score
    GROUP BY name, version
),
associated_models AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        sm.name,
        sm.version,
        sm.status,
        m.L1_model
    FROM status_models AS sm
    JOIN model AS m
      ON m.name = sm.name
     AND m.version = sm.version
),
counts AS (
    SELECT
        status,
        L1_model,
        COUNT(*) AS occurrences
    FROM associated_models
    GROUP BY status, L1_model
)
SELECT status, L1_model, occurrences
FROM counts AS c
WHERE occurrences = (
    SELECT MAX(c2.occurrences)
    FROM counts AS c2
    WHERE c2.status = c.status
)
ORDER BY CASE status WHEN 'strong' THEN 1 WHEN 'soft' THEN 2 END, L1_model

luna.question: Which model category (L1_model) appears the most frequently across all steps and versions when comparing traditional models to the Stack model, and what is the total count of its occurrences?
luna.sql:
SELECT L1_model, COUNT(*) AS occurrences
FROM model
GROUP BY L1_model
ORDER BY occurrences DESC
LIMIT 1

luna.question: What is the average total quantity across all final packaging combinations, considering only the leaf-level items within each combination after fully expanding any nested packaging relationships?
luna.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE
roots(id) AS (
    SELECT p.id
    FROM packaging AS p
    WHERE NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1
        FROM packaging_relations AS r
        WHERE r.contains_id = p.id
    )
),
expanded(root_id, item_id, quantity) AS (
    SELECT id, id, 1
    FROM roots
    UNION ALL
    SELECT e.root_id,
           r.contains_id,
           e.quantity * r.qty
    FROM expanded AS e
    JOIN packaging_relations AS r
      ON r.packaging_id = e.item_id
),
totals AS (
    SELECT e.root_id, SUM(e.quantity) AS total_quantity
    FROM expanded AS e
    WHERE NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1
        FROM packaging_relations AS r
        WHERE r.packaging_id = e.item_id
    )
    GROUP BY e.root_id
)
SELECT AVG(total_quantity)
FROM totals

luna.question: Which top-level packaging containers, meaning those not contained within any other packaging, have any item for which the total quantity accumulated across all nested levels in the hierarchy exceeds 500, and what are the names of both these containers and the corresponding items?
luna.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE top_level AS (
    SELECT p.id, p.name
    FROM packaging AS p
    WHERE NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1
        FROM packaging_relations AS pr
        WHERE pr.contains_id = p.id
    )
),
contents(top_id, item_id, quantity) AS (
    SELECT t.id, pr.contains_id, pr.qty
    FROM top_level AS t
    JOIN packaging_relations AS pr
      ON pr.packaging_id = t.id
    UNION ALL
    SELECT c.top_id, pr.contains_id, c.quantity * pr.qty
    FROM contents AS c
    JOIN packaging_relations AS pr
      ON pr.packaging_id = c.item_id
)
SELECT t.name, p.name
FROM top_level AS t
JOIN (
    SELECT top_id, item_id
    FROM contents
    GROUP BY top_id, item_id
    HAVING SUM(quantity) > 500
) AS c
  ON c.top_id = t.id
JOIN packaging AS p
  ON p.id = c.item_id
ORDER BY t.name, p.name

luna.question: For order 423, identify the product IDs, aisles, and positions from which to pick the exact quantities needed for each order line, ensuring that the total picked quantity for each product matches the cumulative quantities ordered without exceeding the available inventory in warehouse 1. Calculate the quantities to be picked from each location by prioritizing inventory with earlier purchased dates and smaller quantities, and ensure that picking respects the sequence and cumulative quantities of the order lines for products with multiple entries.
luna.sql:
WITH demand AS (
    SELECT
        ol.id AS line_id,
        ol.product_id,
        SUM(ol.qty) OVER (
            PARTITION BY ol.product_id
            ORDER BY ol.id
            ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
        ) - ol.qty AS demand_start,
        SUM(ol.qty) OVER (
            PARTITION BY ol.product_id
            ORDER BY ol.id
            ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
        ) AS demand_end
    FROM orderlines AS ol
    WHERE ol.order_id = 423
),
stock AS (
    SELECT
        i.id AS inventory_id,
        i.product_id,
        l.aisle,
        l.position,
        i.qty AS inventory_qty,
        p.purchased,
        SUM(i.qty) OVER (
            PARTITION BY i.product_id
            ORDER BY p.purchased, i.qty, i.id
            ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
        ) - i.qty AS stock_start,
        SUM(i.qty) OVER (
            PARTITION BY i.product_id
            ORDER BY p.purchased, i.qty, i.id
            ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
        ) AS stock_end
    FROM inventory AS i
    JOIN locations AS l
      ON l.id = i.location_id
    JOIN purchases AS p
      ON p.id = i.purchase_id
    WHERE l.warehouse = 1
),
allocation AS (
    SELECT
        d.line_id,
        d.product_id,
        s.aisle,
        s.position,
        s.purchased,
        s.inventory_qty,
        s.inventory_id,
        MIN(d.demand_end, s.stock_end)
        - MAX(d.demand_start, s.stock_start) AS picked_qty
    FROM demand AS d
    JOIN stock AS s
      ON s.product_id = d.product_id
     AND d.demand_end > s.stock_start
     AND s.stock_end > d.demand_start
)
SELECT product_id, aisle, position, picked_qty
FROM allocation
WHERE picked_qty > 0
ORDER BY line_id, purchased, inventory_qty, inventory_id

luna.question: Calculate the average pick percentage for each product name, using a first-in-first-out approach that selects from inventory locations based on the earliest purchase date and smallest available quantity, ensuring that the picked quantity reflects only the overlapping range between each order’s required quantity and the inventory’s available quantity, and then grouping and ordering the results by product name?
luna.sql:
WITH inventory_ranges AS (
    SELECT
        i.id AS inventory_id,
        i.product_id,
        COALESCE(
            SUM(i.qty) OVER (
                PARTITION BY i.product_id
                ORDER BY pu.purchased, i.qty, i.location_id, i.id
                ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
            ),
            0.0
        ) AS inventory_start,
        SUM(i.qty) OVER (
            PARTITION BY i.product_id
            ORDER BY pu.purchased, i.qty, i.location_id, i.id
            ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
        ) AS inventory_end
    FROM inventory AS i
    JOIN purchases AS pu
      ON pu.id = i.purchase_id
    WHERE i.qty > 0
),
demand_ranges AS (
    SELECT
        ol.id AS line_id,
        ol.product_id,
        ol.qty AS required_qty,
        COALESCE(
            SUM(ol.qty) OVER (
                PARTITION BY ol.product_id
                ORDER BY o.ordered, o.id, ol.id
                ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
            ),
            0.0
        ) AS demand_start,
        SUM(ol.qty) OVER (
            PARTITION BY ol.product_id
            ORDER BY o.ordered, o.id, ol.id
            ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
        ) AS demand_end
    FROM orderlines AS ol
    JOIN orders AS o
      ON o.id = ol.order_id
    WHERE ol.qty > 0
),
line_picks AS (
    SELECT
        d.line_id,
        d.product_id,
        d.required_qty,
        COALESCE(
            SUM(
                CASE
                    WHEN i.inventory_id IS NULL THEN 0.0
                    ELSE MAX(
                        0.0,
                        MIN(d.demand_end, i.inventory_end)
                        - MAX(d.demand_start, i.inventory_start)
                    )
                END
            ),
            0.0
        ) AS picked_qty
    FROM demand_ranges AS d
    LEFT JOIN inventory_ranges AS i
      ON i.product_id = d.product_id
     AND i.inventory_end > d.demand_start
     AND i.inventory_start < d.demand_end
    GROUP BY d.line_id, d.product_id, d.required_qty
)
SELECT
    p.name AS product_name,
    AVG(100.0 * lp.picked_qty / NULLIF(lp.required_qty, 0)) AS average_pick_percentage
FROM line_picks AS lp
JOIN products AS p
  ON p.id = lp.product_id
GROUP BY p.name
ORDER BY p.name

luna.question: Which products were picked for order 421, and what is the average number of units picked for each product, using FIFO (First-In, First-Out) method?
luna.sql:
WITH fifo_picks AS (
    SELECT pl.product_id,
           pl.qty,
           pu.purchased
    FROM picking_line AS pl
    JOIN inventory AS i
      ON i.location_id = pl.location_id
     AND i.product_id = pl.product_id
    JOIN purchases AS pu
      ON pu.id = i.purchase_id
    WHERE pl.order_id = 421
)
SELECT p.name,
       AVG(fp.qty)
FROM fifo_picks AS fp
JOIN products AS p
  ON p.id = fp.product_id
GROUP BY p.id, p.name
ORDER BY MIN(fp.purchased), p.name, p.id

luna.question: Based on monthly sales data starting in January 2016 and using a centered moving average to adjust for seasonality, which products had a seasonality-adjusted sales ratio that stayed consistently above 2 for every month in the year 2017?
luna.sql:
WITH numbered AS (
    SELECT
        product_id,
        mth,
        qty,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY product_id
            ORDER BY mth
        ) AS month_no
    FROM monthly_sales
),
moving AS (
    SELECT
        product_id,
        mth,
        qty,
        month_no,
        AVG(qty) OVER (
            PARTITION BY product_id
            ORDER BY month_no
            ROWS BETWEEN 5 PRECEDING AND 6 FOLLOWING
        ) AS avg_5_before_6_after,
        AVG(qty) OVER (
            PARTITION BY product_id
            ORDER BY month_no
            ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND 5 FOLLOWING
        ) AS avg_6_before_5_after
    FROM numbered
),
ratios AS (
    SELECT
        product_id,
        mth,
        qty / ((avg_5_before_6_after + avg_6_before_5_after) / 2.0) AS sales_to_cma
    FROM moving
    WHERE month_no BETWEEN 7 AND 30
      AND mth >= '2017-01-01'
      AND mth < '2018-01-01'
)
SELECT p.name
FROM ratios AS r
JOIN products AS p ON p.id = r.product_id
GROUP BY r.product_id, p.name
HAVING COUNT(*) = 12
   AND MIN(r.sales_to_cma) > 2
ORDER BY p.name

luna.question: What is the average forecasted annual sales for products 4160 and 7790 during 2018, using monthly sales data starting from January 2016 for the first 36 months, applying seasonality adjustments from time steps 7 through 30, and employing a weighted regression method to estimate sales?
luna.sql:
WITH raw AS (
    SELECT
        ms.product_id,
        ms.mth,
        ms.qty,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY ms.product_id
            ORDER BY ms.mth
        ) AS t
    FROM monthly_sales AS ms
    WHERE ms.product_id IN (4160, 7790)
      AND ms.mth >= '2016-01-01'
      AND ms.mth < '2019-01-01'
),
data AS (
    SELECT product_id, mth, qty, t
    FROM raw
    WHERE t <= 36
),
moving AS (
    SELECT
        product_id,
        mth,
        qty,
        t,
        AVG(qty) OVER (
            PARTITION BY product_id
            ORDER BY t
            ROWS BETWEEN 5 PRECEDING AND 6 FOLLOWING
        ) AS ma_1,
        AVG(qty) OVER (
            PARTITION BY product_id
            ORDER BY t
            ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND 5 FOLLOWING
        ) AS ma_2
    FROM data
),
ratio_data AS (
    SELECT
        product_id,
        mth,
        t,
        qty,
        qty / NULLIF((ma_1 + ma_2) / 2.0, 0.0) AS sales_to_cma
    FROM moving
    WHERE t BETWEEN 7 AND 30
),
seasonal AS (
    SELECT
        product_id,
        strftime('%m', mth) AS month_no,
        AVG(sales_to_cma) AS seasonal_index
    FROM ratio_data
    GROUP BY product_id, strftime('%m', mth)
),
adjusted AS (
    SELECT
        d.product_id,
        d.mth,
        d.t,
        s.seasonal_index,
        d.qty / NULLIF(s.seasonal_index, 0.0) AS deseasonalized_qty
    FROM data AS d
    JOIN seasonal AS s
      ON s.product_id = d.product_id
     AND s.month_no = strftime('%m', d.mth)
),
weighted_data AS (
    SELECT
        product_id,
        t,
        t * 1.0 AS weight,
        deseasonalized_qty
    FROM adjusted
    WHERE deseasonalized_qty IS NOT NULL
),
weighted_sums AS (
    SELECT
        product_id,
        SUM(weight) AS sw,
        SUM(weight * t) AS swx,
        SUM(weight * deseasonalized_qty) AS swy,
        SUM(weight * t * t) AS swxx,
        SUM(weight * t * deseasonalized_qty) AS swxy
    FROM weighted_data
    GROUP BY product_id
),
slope_calc AS (
    SELECT
        product_id,
        sw,
        swx,
        swy,
        (sw * swxy - swx * swy) /
            NULLIF(sw * swxx - swx * swx, 0.0) AS slope
    FROM weighted_sums
),
coefficients AS (
    SELECT
        product_id,
        slope,
        (swy - slope * swx) / NULLIF(sw, 0.0) AS intercept
    FROM slope_calc
),
annual_forecasts AS (
    SELECT
        a.product_id,
        SUM((c.intercept + c.slope * a.t) * a.seasonal_index) AS annual_sales
    FROM adjusted AS a
    JOIN coefficients AS c
      ON c.product_id = a.product_id
    WHERE a.t BETWEEN 25 AND 36
      AND a.mth >= '2018-01-01'
      AND a.mth < '2019-01-01'
    GROUP BY a.product_id
)
SELECT AVG(annual_sales)
FROM annual_forecasts

luna.question: Using a recursive monthly inventory adjustment model starting from December 2018 inventory levels, where we restock a product if its ending inventory drops below the minimum required level, determine for each product the month in 2019 where the absolute difference between its ending inventory and the minimum required level is the smallest, and return the product_id, that month, and the absolute difference.
luna.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE inventory_levels(product_id, mth, ending_inventory, qty_minimum, qty_purchase) AS (
    SELECT
        pm.product_id,
        '2018-12-01',
        COALESCE(SUM(i.qty), 0),
        pm.qty_minimum,
        pm.qty_purchase
    FROM product_minimums AS pm
    LEFT JOIN inventory AS i
        ON i.product_id = pm.product_id
    GROUP BY pm.product_id, pm.qty_minimum, pm.qty_purchase
    UNION ALL
    SELECT
        il.product_id,
        date(il.mth, '+1 month'),
        CASE
            WHEN il.ending_inventory - COALESCE(ms.qty, 0) < il.qty_minimum
            THEN il.ending_inventory - COALESCE(ms.qty, 0) + il.qty_purchase
            ELSE il.ending_inventory - COALESCE(ms.qty, 0)
        END,
        il.qty_minimum,
        il.qty_purchase
    FROM inventory_levels AS il
    LEFT JOIN monthly_sales AS ms
        ON ms.product_id = il.product_id
       AND date(ms.mth) = date(il.mth, '+1 month')
    WHERE il.mth < '2019-12-01'
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT
        product_id,
        mth,
        ABS(ending_inventory - qty_minimum) AS difference,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY product_id
            ORDER BY ABS(ending_inventory - qty_minimum), mth
        ) AS rn
    FROM inventory_levels
    WHERE mth BETWEEN '2019-01-01' AND '2019-12-01'
)
SELECT product_id, mth, difference
FROM ranked
WHERE rn = 1
ORDER BY product_id

luna.question: Analyze the soccer match dataset to determine the champion team for each season across all countries and leagues, awarding 3 points for every win, 1 point for every tie, and 0 points for every loss. For each season, return the champion’s team name, the league, the country, and the total points accumulated.
luna.sql:
WITH team_points AS (
    SELECT
        m.season,
        m.league_id,
        m.home_team_api_id AS team_api_id,
        SUM(
            CASE
                WHEN m.home_team_goal > m.away_team_goal THEN 3
                WHEN m.home_team_goal = m.away_team_goal THEN 1
                ELSE 0
            END
        ) AS points
    FROM "Match" AS m
    GROUP BY m.season, m.league_id, m.home_team_api_id
    UNION ALL
    SELECT
        m.season,
        m.league_id,
        m.away_team_api_id AS team_api_id,
        SUM(
            CASE
                WHEN m.away_team_goal > m.home_team_goal THEN 3
                WHEN m.away_team_goal = m.home_team_goal THEN 1
                ELSE 0
            END
        ) AS points
    FROM "Match" AS m
    GROUP BY m.season, m.league_id, m.away_team_api_id
),
team_totals AS (
    SELECT
        season,
        league_id,
        team_api_id,
        SUM(points) AS total_points
    FROM team_points
    GROUP BY season, league_id, team_api_id
),
ranked_teams AS (
    SELECT
        season,
        league_id,
        team_api_id,
        total_points,
        RANK() OVER (
            PARTITION BY season, league_id
            ORDER BY total_points DESC
        ) AS team_rank
    FROM team_totals
)
SELECT
    t.team_long_name,
    l.name,
    c.name,
    r.total_points
FROM ranked_teams AS r
JOIN Team AS t
    ON t.team_api_id = r.team_api_id
JOIN League AS l
    ON l.id = r.league_id
JOIN Country AS c
    ON c.id = l.country_id
WHERE r.team_rank = 1
ORDER BY r.season, c.name, l.name, t.team_long_name

luna.question: For veg whsle data, can you generate a summary of our items' loss rates? Include the average loss rate, and also break down the count of items that are below, above, and within one standard deviation from this average.
luna.sql:
WITH stats AS (
    SELECT
        AVG("loss_rate_%") AS average_loss_rate,
        SQRT(
            AVG("loss_rate_%" * "loss_rate_%") -
            AVG("loss_rate_%") * AVG("loss_rate_%")
        ) AS standard_deviation
    FROM veg_loss_rate_df
)
SELECT
    stats.average_loss_rate,
    SUM(CASE WHEN v."loss_rate_%" < stats.average_loss_rate - stats.standard_deviation THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS below_one_standard_deviation,
    SUM(CASE WHEN v."loss_rate_%" > stats.average_loss_rate + stats.standard_deviation THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS above_one_standard_deviation,
    SUM(CASE WHEN v."loss_rate_%" BETWEEN stats.average_loss_rate - stats.standard_deviation AND stats.average_loss_rate + stats.standard_deviation THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS within_one_standard_deviation
FROM veg_loss_rate_df AS v
CROSS JOIN stats

luna.question: For veg whsle data, can you analyze our financial performance over the years 2020 to 2023? I need insights into the average wholesale price, maximum wholesale price, minimum wholesale price, wholesale price difference, total wholesale price, total selling price, average loss rate, total loss, and profit for each category within each year. Round all calculated values to two decimal places.
luna.sql:
WITH item_info AS (
    SELECT
        c.item_code,
        c.category_name,
        l."loss_rate_%" AS loss_rate
    FROM veg_cat AS c
    LEFT JOIN veg_loss_rate_df AS l
        ON l.item_code = c.item_code
),
wholesale AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        i.item_code,
        i.category_name,
        i.loss_rate,
        w."whsle_date" AS whsle_date,
        CAST(substr(w."whsle_date", 1, 4) AS INTEGER) AS yr,
        CAST(w."whsle_px_rmb-kg" AS REAL) AS wholesale_price
    FROM veg_whsle_df AS w
    JOIN item_info AS i
        ON i.item_code = w.item_code
    WHERE CAST(substr(w."whsle_date", 1, 4) AS INTEGER) BETWEEN 2020 AND 2023
),
price_stats AS (
    SELECT
        category_name,
        yr,
        AVG(wholesale_price) AS avg_wholesale_price,
        MAX(wholesale_price) AS max_wholesale_price,
        MIN(wholesale_price) AS min_wholesale_price,
        MAX(wholesale_price) - MIN(wholesale_price) AS wholesale_price_difference
    FROM wholesale
    GROUP BY category_name, yr
),
loss_stats AS (
    SELECT
        category_name,
        yr,
        AVG(loss_rate) AS avg_loss_rate
    FROM (
        SELECT DISTINCT
            category_name,
            item_code,
            yr,
            loss_rate
        FROM wholesale
        WHERE loss_rate IS NOT NULL
    ) AS distinct_item_rates
    GROUP BY category_name, yr
),
transaction_detail AS (
    SELECT
        w.category_name,
        w.yr,
        CASE
            WHEN lower(trim(COALESCE(t."sale/return", ''))) IN ('return', 'returned', '退货', '退货单')
                THEN -ABS(CAST(t."qty_sold(kg)" AS REAL))
            WHEN lower(trim(COALESCE(t."sale/return", ''))) IN ('sale', 'sold', '销售', '销售单')
                THEN ABS(CAST(t."qty_sold(kg)" AS REAL))
            ELSE CAST(t."qty_sold(kg)" AS REAL)
        END AS quantity,
        CAST(t."unit_selling_px_rmb/kg" AS REAL) AS selling_price,
        COALESCE(CAST(t."discount(%)" AS REAL), 0.0) AS discount_pct,
        w.wholesale_price,
        COALESCE(w.loss_rate, 0.0) AS loss_rate
    FROM veg_txn_df AS t
    JOIN wholesale AS w
        ON w.item_code = t.item_code
       AND w.whsle_date = t.txn_date
),
financials AS (
    SELECT
        category_name,
        yr,
        SUM(quantity * wholesale_price) AS total_wholesale_price,
        SUM(quantity * selling_price * (1.0 - discount_pct / 100.0)) AS total_selling_price,
        SUM(quantity * wholesale_price * loss_rate / 100.0) AS total_loss
    FROM transaction_detail
    GROUP BY category_name, yr
)
SELECT
    p.yr,
    p.category_name,
    ROUND(p.avg_wholesale_price, 2),
    ROUND(p.max_wholesale_price, 2),
    ROUND(p.min_wholesale_price, 2),
    ROUND(p.wholesale_price_difference, 2),
    ROUND(COALESCE(f.total_wholesale_price, 0.0), 2),
    ROUND(COALESCE(f.total_selling_price, 0.0), 2),
    ROUND(COALESCE(l.avg_loss_rate, 0.0), 2),
    ROUND(COALESCE(f.total_loss, 0.0), 2),
    ROUND(
        COALESCE(f.total_selling_price, 0.0)
        - COALESCE(f.total_wholesale_price, 0.0)
        - COALESCE(f.total_loss, 0.0),
        2
    )
FROM price_stats AS p
LEFT JOIN financials AS f
    ON f.category_name = p.category_name
   AND f.yr = p.yr
LEFT JOIN loss_stats AS l
    ON l.category_name = p.category_name
   AND l.yr = p.yr
ORDER BY p.yr, p.category_name

luna.question: Prepare a comprehensive performance report on our sellers, focusing on total sales, average item price, average review scores, and packing times. Ensure that the report includes only those sellers who have sold a quantity of more than 100 products and highlight the product category names in English with the highest sales volume.
luna.sql:
WITH qualified_sellers AS (
    SELECT
        seller_id,
        COUNT(*) AS products_sold,
        SUM(price) AS total_sales,
        AVG(price) AS average_item_price
    FROM order_items
    GROUP BY seller_id
    HAVING COUNT(*) > 100
),
review_scores AS (
    SELECT
        order_id,
        AVG(review_score) AS average_review_score
    FROM order_reviews
    GROUP BY order_id
),
seller_orders AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        oi.seller_id,
        oi.order_id
    FROM order_items AS oi
    INNER JOIN qualified_sellers AS qs
        ON qs.seller_id = oi.seller_id
),
seller_service_metrics AS (
    SELECT
        so.seller_id,
        AVG(rs.average_review_score) AS average_review_score,
        AVG(
            julianday(o.order_delivered_carrier_date) -
            julianday(COALESCE(o.order_approved_at, o.order_purchase_timestamp))
        ) AS average_packing_time_days
    FROM seller_orders AS so
    LEFT JOIN orders AS o
        ON o.order_id = so.order_id
    LEFT JOIN review_scores AS rs
        ON rs.order_id = so.order_id
    GROUP BY so.seller_id
),
category_sales AS (
    SELECT
        oi.seller_id,
        pct.product_category_name_english,
        COUNT(*) AS category_sales_volume
    FROM order_items AS oi
    INNER JOIN qualified_sellers AS qs
        ON qs.seller_id = oi.seller_id
    INNER JOIN products AS p
        ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
    INNER JOIN product_category_name_translation AS pct
        ON pct.product_category_name = p.product_category_name
    GROUP BY
        oi.seller_id,
        pct.product_category_name_english
),
ranked_categories AS (
    SELECT
        seller_id,
        product_category_name_english,
        category_sales_volume,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY seller_id
            ORDER BY category_sales_volume DESC, product_category_name_english
        ) AS category_rank
    FROM category_sales
)
SELECT
    qs.seller_id,
    qs.products_sold,
    qs.total_sales,
    qs.average_item_price,
    ssm.average_review_score,
    ssm.average_packing_time_days,
    rc.product_category_name_english,
    rc.category_sales_volume
FROM qualified_sellers AS qs
LEFT JOIN seller_service_metrics AS ssm
    ON ssm.seller_id = qs.seller_id
LEFT JOIN ranked_categories AS rc
    ON rc.seller_id = qs.seller_id
   AND rc.category_rank = 1
ORDER BY qs.total_sales DESC, qs.seller_id

luna.question: For weekly-sales data, I need an analysis of our sales performance around mid-June for the years 2018, 2019, and 2020. Specifically, calculate the percentage change in sales between the four weeks leading up to June 15 and the four weeks following June 15 for each year.
luna.sql:
WITH periods(year, anchor_date) AS (
    VALUES
        (2018, '2018-06-15'),
        (2019, '2019-06-15'),
        (2020, '2020-06-15')
),
period_sales AS (
    SELECT
        p.year,
        SUM(CASE
                WHEN date(w.week_date) >= date(p.anchor_date, '-28 days')
                 AND date(w.week_date) < date(p.anchor_date)
                THEN w.sales
                ELSE 0
            END) AS sales_before,
        SUM(CASE
                WHEN date(w.week_date) > date(p.anchor_date)
                 AND date(w.week_date) <= date(p.anchor_date, '+28 days')
                THEN w.sales
                ELSE 0
            END) AS sales_after
    FROM periods AS p
    LEFT JOIN weekly_sales AS w
      ON date(w.week_date) BETWEEN date(p.anchor_date, '-28 days')
                               AND date(p.anchor_date, '+28 days')
    GROUP BY p.year
)
SELECT
    year,
    sales_before,
    sales_after,
    100.0 * (sales_after - sales_before) / NULLIF(sales_before, 0) AS percentage_change
FROM period_sales
ORDER BY year

luna.question: Analyze the average percentage change in sales between the 12 weeks before and after June 15, 2020, for each attribute type: region, platform, age band, demographic, and customer type. For each attribute type, calculate the average percentage change in sales across all its attribute values. Identify the attribute type with the highest negative impact on sales and provide its average percentage change in sales.
luna.sql:
WITH attribute_sales AS (
    SELECT 'region' AS attribute_type, region AS attribute_value, week_date_formatted, sales
    FROM cleaned_weekly_sales
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'platform', platform, week_date_formatted, sales
    FROM cleaned_weekly_sales
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'age_band', age_band, week_date_formatted, sales
    FROM cleaned_weekly_sales
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'demographic', demographic, week_date_formatted, sales
    FROM cleaned_weekly_sales
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'customer_type', customer_type, week_date_formatted, sales
    FROM cleaned_weekly_sales
),
attribute_changes AS (
    SELECT
        attribute_type,
        attribute_value,
        SUM(CASE
                WHEN week_date_formatted < date('2020-06-15') THEN sales
                ELSE 0
            END) AS before_sales,
        SUM(CASE
                WHEN week_date_formatted >= date('2020-06-15') THEN sales
                ELSE 0
            END) AS after_sales
    FROM attribute_sales
    WHERE attribute_value IS NOT NULL
      AND week_date_formatted >= date('2020-06-15', '-84 days')
      AND week_date_formatted < date('2020-06-15', '+84 days')
    GROUP BY attribute_type, attribute_value
),
attribute_type_changes AS (
    SELECT
        attribute_type,
        AVG(100.0 * (after_sales - before_sales) / NULLIF(before_sales, 0)) AS average_percentage_change
    FROM attribute_changes
    GROUP BY attribute_type
)
SELECT attribute_type, average_percentage_change
FROM attribute_type_changes
ORDER BY average_percentage_change ASC
LIMIT 1

luna.question: How many unique sessions visited the /regist/input page and then the /regist/confirm page, in that order?
luna.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT i.session)
FROM activity_log AS i
JOIN activity_log AS c
  ON c.session = i.session
 AND i.stamp < c.stamp
WHERE i.path = '/regist/input'
  AND c.path = '/regist/confirm'

luna.question: Using the activity log table, compute the total number of unique user sessions where each web page appears as either a landing page (the first page visited in a session based on timestamp) or an exit page (the last page visited in a session based on timestamp), or both. Count each session only once per page even if the page serves as both landing and exit for that session.
luna.sql:
WITH ranked AS (
    SELECT
        session,
        path,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY session ORDER BY stamp) AS first_rank,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY session ORDER BY stamp DESC) AS last_rank
    FROM activity_log
),
page_sessions AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT session, path
    FROM ranked
    WHERE first_rank = 1 OR last_rank = 1
)
SELECT path, COUNT(*) AS session_count
FROM page_sessions
GROUP BY path
ORDER BY path

luna.question: Which three distinct third-page visits are most frequently observed immediately after two consecutive visits to the '/detail' page, and how many times does each third-page visit occur?
luna.sql:
WITH ordered_visits AS (
    SELECT
        session,
        url,
        LEAD(url, 1) OVER (
            PARTITION BY session
            ORDER BY stamp
        ) AS next_url,
        LEAD(url, 2) OVER (
            PARTITION BY session
            ORDER BY stamp
        ) AS third_url
    FROM read_log
)
SELECT
    third_url,
    COUNT(*) AS visit_count
FROM ordered_visits
WHERE url = '/detail'
  AND next_url = '/detail'
  AND third_url IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY third_url
ORDER BY visit_count DESC, third_url
LIMIT 3

luna.question: How many users are there in each age category (20s, 30s, 40s, 50s, and others)?
luna.sql:
WITH age_groups(category, sort_order) AS (
    VALUES ('20s', 1), ('30s', 2), ('40s', 3), ('50s', 4), ('others', 5)
),
categorized AS (
    SELECT CASE
        WHEN age BETWEEN 20 AND 29 THEN '20s'
        WHEN age BETWEEN 30 AND 39 THEN '30s'
        WHEN age BETWEEN 40 AND 49 THEN '40s'
        WHEN age BETWEEN 50 AND 59 THEN '50s'
        ELSE 'others'
    END AS category
    FROM (
        SELECT CAST(strftime('%Y', 'now') AS INTEGER)
             - CAST(strftime('%Y', birth_date) AS INTEGER)
             - CASE WHEN strftime('%m-%d', 'now') < strftime('%m-%d', birth_date) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS age
        FROM mst_users
    )
)
SELECT g.category, COUNT(c.category)
FROM age_groups AS g
LEFT JOIN categorized AS c ON c.category = g.category
GROUP BY g.category, g.sort_order
ORDER BY g.sort_order

luna.question: For each user session in the activity log table, identify the number of events that occurred before the first '/detail' click or '/complete' conversion, counting only events that have a non-empty search type. Find the sessions with the minimum count of such pre-click/pre-conversion events. If multiple sessions share this minimum count, include all of them in the results. Return each qualifying session along with the corresponding path and search type.
luna.sql:
WITH first_events AS (
    SELECT session, stamp, path, search_type
    FROM (
        SELECT
            session,
            stamp,
            path,
            search_type,
            ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
                PARTITION BY session
                ORDER BY stamp,
                         CASE WHEN action = 'click' THEN 1 ELSE 2 END,
                         path,
                         search_type
            ) AS rn
        FROM activity_log
        WHERE (action = 'click' AND path = '/detail')
           OR (action = 'conversion' AND path = '/complete')
    )
    WHERE rn = 1
),
session_counts AS (
    SELECT
        f.session,
        f.path,
        f.search_type,
        COUNT(a.stamp) AS event_count
    FROM first_events AS f
    LEFT JOIN activity_log AS a
      ON a.session = f.session
     AND a.stamp < f.stamp
     AND a.search_type IS NOT NULL
     AND a.search_type <> ''
    GROUP BY f.session, f.stamp, f.path, f.search_type
)
SELECT session, path, search_type
FROM session_counts
WHERE event_count = (SELECT MIN(event_count) FROM session_counts)

luna.question: Considering all races where pit stop data is available, and focusing on instances when a driver was not behind another car on the previous lap but is behind on the current lap (accounting for retirements, pit-stop entries, pit-stop exits, and race starts), how many times has each type of overtake occurred in Formula 1?
luna.sql:
WITH type_list(label) AS (VALUES ('R'), ('P'), ('S'), ('T')),
typical_pit AS (
    SELECT AVG(CAST(ps.milliseconds AS REAL)) AS typical_ms
    FROM pit_stops AS ps
    JOIN races_ext AS re
      ON re.race_id = ps.race_id
    WHERE re.is_pit_data_available = 1
      AND ps.milliseconds > 0
),
candidates AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
           lp1.race_id,
           lp1.lap,
           lp1.driver_id AS overtaken_driver_id,
           lp2.driver_id AS overtaking_driver_id,
           r1.grid AS overtaken_grid,
           r2.grid AS overtaking_grid
    FROM lap_positions AS lp1
    JOIN lap_positions AS lp2
      ON lp2.race_id = lp1.race_id
     AND lp2.lap = lp1.lap
     AND lp2.driver_id <> lp1.driver_id
    JOIN races_ext AS re
      ON re.race_id = lp1.race_id
     AND re.is_pit_data_available = 1
    JOIN results AS r1
      ON r1.race_id = lp1.race_id
     AND r1.driver_id = lp1.driver_id
    JOIN results AS r2
      ON r2.race_id = lp2.race_id
     AND r2.driver_id = lp2.driver_id
    LEFT JOIN lap_positions AS prev1
      ON prev1.race_id = lp1.race_id
     AND prev1.driver_id = lp1.driver_id
     AND prev1.lap = lp1.lap - 1
    LEFT JOIN lap_positions AS prev2
      ON prev2.race_id = lp2.race_id
     AND prev2.driver_id = lp2.driver_id
     AND prev2.lap = lp2.lap - 1
    WHERE lp1.position IS NOT NULL
      AND lp2.position IS NOT NULL
      AND lp1.position > lp2.position
      AND (
            (
                lp1.lap = 1
                AND r1.grid > 0
                AND r2.grid > 0
                AND r1.grid <= r2.grid
            )
            OR
            (
                lp1.lap > 1
                AND prev1.position IS NOT NULL
                AND prev2.position IS NOT NULL
                AND prev1.position <= prev2.position
            )
          )
),
classified AS (
    SELECT c.*,
           CASE
               WHEN EXISTS (
                   SELECT 1
                   FROM retirements AS rt
                   WHERE rt.race_id = c.race_id
                     AND rt.driver_id = c.overtaken_driver_id
                     AND rt.lap = c.lap
               ) THEN 'R'
               WHEN EXISTS (
                   SELECT 1
                   FROM pit_stops AS ps
                   WHERE ps.race_id = c.race_id
                     AND ps.driver_id = c.overtaken_driver_id
                     AND ps.lap = c.lap
               )
               OR (
                   EXISTS (
                       SELECT 1
                       FROM pit_stops AS ps
                       WHERE ps.race_id = c.race_id
                         AND ps.driver_id = c.overtaken_driver_id
                         AND ps.lap = c.lap - 1
                   )
                   AND EXISTS (
                       SELECT 1
                       FROM lap_times_ext AS lt1
                       JOIN lap_times_ext AS lt2
                         ON lt2.race_id = lt1.race_id
                        AND lt2.lap = lt1.lap
                        AND lt2.driver_id = c.overtaking_driver_id
                       CROSS JOIN typical_pit AS tp
                       WHERE lt1.race_id = c.race_id
                         AND lt1.lap = c.lap
                         AND lt1.driver_id = c.overtaken_driver_id
                         AND lt1.running_milliseconds IS NOT NULL
                         AND lt2.running_milliseconds IS NOT NULL
                         AND ABS(
                               CAST(lt1.running_milliseconds AS REAL) -
                               CAST(lt2.running_milliseconds AS REAL)
                             ) < tp.typical_ms
                   )
               ) THEN 'P'
               WHEN c.lap = 1
                AND c.overtaken_grid > 0
                AND c.overtaking_grid > 0
                AND ABS(c.overtaken_grid - c.overtaking_grid) <= 2 THEN 'S'
               ELSE 'T'
           END AS overtake_type
    FROM candidates AS c
)
SELECT tl.label,
       COUNT(cl.overtake_type) AS overtake_count
FROM type_list AS tl
LEFT JOIN classified AS cl
  ON cl.overtake_type = tl.label
GROUP BY tl.label
ORDER BY CASE tl.label
             WHEN 'R' THEN 1
             WHEN 'P' THEN 2
             WHEN 'S' THEN 3
             WHEN 'T' THEN 4
         END

luna.question: In the first five laps of the race, how many overtakes occurred in each category—retirements, pit stops, start-related overtakes, and standard on-track passes?
luna.sql:
WITH
positions AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT race_id, driver_id, lap, position
    FROM lap_positions
    WHERE lap BETWEEN 1 AND 5
      AND position IS NOT NULL
      AND position > 0
),
overtakes AS (
    SELECT
        a.race_id,
        a.lap,
        a.driver_id AS overtaker_id,
        b.driver_id AS overtaken_id
    FROM positions AS a
    JOIN positions AS b
      ON b.race_id = a.race_id
     AND b.lap = a.lap
     AND b.driver_id <> a.driver_id
    JOIN results AS ga
      ON ga.race_id = a.race_id
     AND ga.driver_id = a.driver_id
    JOIN results AS gb
      ON gb.race_id = b.race_id
     AND gb.driver_id = b.driver_id
    WHERE a.lap = 1
      AND a.position < b.position
      AND ga.grid > 0
      AND gb.grid > 0
      AND ga.grid > gb.grid
    UNION
    SELECT
        a.race_id,
        a.lap,
        a.driver_id AS overtaker_id,
        b.driver_id AS overtaken_id
    FROM positions AS a
    JOIN positions AS b
      ON b.race_id = a.race_id
     AND b.lap = a.lap
     AND b.driver_id <> a.driver_id
    JOIN positions AS ap
      ON ap.race_id = a.race_id
     AND ap.driver_id = a.driver_id
     AND ap.lap = a.lap - 1
    JOIN positions AS bp
      ON bp.race_id = b.race_id
     AND bp.driver_id = b.driver_id
     AND bp.lap = b.lap - 1
    WHERE a.lap BETWEEN 2 AND 5
      AND ap.position > bp.position
      AND a.position < b.position
),
lap_clock AS (
    SELECT
        race_id,
        driver_id,
        lap,
        MAX(running_milliseconds) AS running_milliseconds
    FROM lap_times_ext
    GROUP BY race_id, driver_id, lap
),
event_data AS (
    SELECT
        o.race_id,
        o.lap,
        o.overtaker_id,
        o.overtaken_id,
        ca.running_milliseconds AS overtaker_ms,
        cb.running_milliseconds AS overtaken_ms,
        ga.grid AS overtaker_grid,
        gb.grid AS overtaken_grid
    FROM overtakes AS o
    LEFT JOIN lap_clock AS ca
      ON ca.race_id = o.race_id
     AND ca.driver_id = o.overtaker_id
     AND ca.lap = o.lap
    LEFT JOIN lap_clock AS cb
      ON cb.race_id = o.race_id
     AND cb.driver_id = o.overtaken_id
     AND cb.lap = o.lap
    LEFT JOIN results AS ga
      ON ga.race_id = o.race_id
     AND ga.driver_id = o.overtaker_id
    LEFT JOIN results AS gb
      ON gb.race_id = o.race_id
     AND gb.driver_id = o.overtaken_id
),
typical_pit AS (
    SELECT AVG(CAST(milliseconds AS REAL)) AS typical_ms
    FROM pit_stops
    WHERE milliseconds IS NOT NULL
),
classified AS (
    SELECT
        CASE
            WHEN EXISTS (
                SELECT 1
                FROM retirements AS r
                WHERE r.race_id = e.race_id
                  AND r.driver_id = e.overtaken_id
                  AND r.lap = e.lap
            ) THEN 'R'
            WHEN EXISTS (
                SELECT 1
                FROM pit_stops AS p
                WHERE p.race_id = e.race_id
                  AND p.driver_id = e.overtaken_id
                  AND p.lap = e.lap
            ) THEN 'P'
            WHEN EXISTS (
                SELECT 1
                FROM pit_stops AS p
                WHERE p.race_id = e.race_id
                  AND p.driver_id = e.overtaken_id
                  AND p.lap = e.lap - 1
            )
            AND e.overtaker_ms IS NOT NULL
            AND e.overtaken_ms IS NOT NULL
            AND t.typical_ms IS NOT NULL
            AND ABS(
                CAST(e.overtaker_ms AS REAL) -
                CAST(e.overtaken_ms AS REAL)
            ) < t.typical_ms THEN 'P'
            WHEN e.lap = 1
             AND e.overtaker_grid - e.overtaken_grid BETWEEN 1 AND 2 THEN 'S'
            ELSE 'T'
        END AS category
    FROM event_data AS e
    CROSS JOIN typical_pit AS t
),
categories(ord, category) AS (
    VALUES
        (1, 'R'),
        (2, 'P'),
        (3, 'S'),
        (4, 'T')
)
SELECT
    c.category,
    COUNT(x.category) AS overtake_count
FROM categories AS c
LEFT JOIN classified AS x
  ON x.category = c.category
GROUP BY c.ord, c.category
ORDER BY c.ord

luna.question: In Formula 1 seasons since 2001, considering only drivers who scored points in a season, which five constructors have had the most seasons where their drivers scored the fewest total points among all point-scoring drivers in that season?
luna.sql:
WITH all_points AS (
    SELECT race_id, driver_id, constructor_id, points
    FROM results
    UNION ALL
    SELECT race_id, driver_id, constructor_id, points
    FROM sprint_results
),
driver_season_totals AS (
    SELECT r.year, p.driver_id, SUM(p.points) AS total_points
    FROM all_points AS p
    JOIN races AS r ON r.race_id = p.race_id
    WHERE r.year >= 2001
    GROUP BY r.year, p.driver_id
    HAVING SUM(p.points) > 0
),
season_minima AS (
    SELECT year, MIN(total_points) AS min_points
    FROM driver_season_totals
    GROUP BY year
),
minimum_drivers AS (
    SELECT d.year, d.driver_id
    FROM driver_season_totals AS d
    JOIN season_minima AS m
      ON m.year = d.year
     AND m.min_points = d.total_points
),
driver_constructor_seasons AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT r.year, p.driver_id, p.constructor_id
    FROM all_points AS p
    JOIN races AS r ON r.race_id = p.race_id
    WHERE r.year >= 2001
      AND p.points > 0
)
SELECT c.name, COUNT(DISTINCT md.year) AS seasons
FROM minimum_drivers AS md
JOIN driver_constructor_seasons AS dcs
  ON dcs.year = md.year
 AND dcs.driver_id = md.driver_id
JOIN constructors AS c
  ON c.constructor_id = dcs.constructor_id
GROUP BY c.constructor_id, c.name
ORDER BY seasons DESC, c.name
LIMIT 5

luna.question: For each year, which driver and which constructor scored the most points? I want the full name of each driver.
luna.sql:
WITH final_races AS (
    SELECT r.year, r.race_id
    FROM races AS r
    WHERE r.round = (
        SELECT MAX(r2.round)
        FROM races AS r2
        WHERE r2.year = r.year
    )
),
driver_points AS (
    SELECT fr.year, ds.driver_id, MAX(ds.points) AS points
    FROM final_races AS fr
    JOIN driver_standings AS ds ON ds.race_id = fr.race_id
    GROUP BY fr.year, ds.driver_id
),
driver_winners AS (
    SELECT dp.year, dp.driver_id
    FROM driver_points AS dp
    WHERE dp.points = (
        SELECT MAX(dp2.points)
        FROM driver_points AS dp2
        WHERE dp2.year = dp.year
    )
),
constructor_points AS (
    SELECT fr.year, cs.constructor_id, MAX(cs.points) AS points
    FROM final_races AS fr
    JOIN constructor_standings AS cs ON cs.race_id = fr.race_id
    GROUP BY fr.year, cs.constructor_id
),
constructor_winners AS (
    SELECT cp.year, cp.constructor_id
    FROM constructor_points AS cp
    WHERE cp.points = (
        SELECT MAX(cp2.points)
        FROM constructor_points AS cp2
        WHERE cp2.year = cp.year
    )
)
SELECT dw.year, d.full_name, c.name
FROM driver_winners AS dw
JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driver_id = dw.driver_id
JOIN constructor_winners AS cw ON cw.year = dw.year
JOIN constructors AS c ON c.constructor_id = cw.constructor_id
ORDER BY dw.year, d.full_name, c.name

luna.question: Using only the data from the ‘results’ table, find the three years in which the sum of the highest total points earned by any driver and the highest total points earned by any constructor in that year (both calculated by summing up points from the ‘results’ table) is smallest, and list those three years in order of ascending total.
luna.sql:
WITH driver_totals AS (
    SELECT r.year, res.driver_id, SUM(res.points) AS total_points
    FROM races AS r
    JOIN results AS res ON res.race_id = r.race_id
    GROUP BY r.year, res.driver_id
),
constructor_totals AS (
    SELECT r.year, res.constructor_id, SUM(res.points) AS total_points
    FROM races AS r
    JOIN results AS res ON res.race_id = r.race_id
    GROUP BY r.year, res.constructor_id
),
yearly_totals AS (
    SELECT d.year,
           MAX(d.total_points) + MAX(c.total_points) AS total_points
    FROM driver_totals AS d
    JOIN constructor_totals AS c ON c.year = d.year
    GROUP BY d.year
)
SELECT year
FROM yearly_totals
ORDER BY total_points ASC, year ASC
LIMIT 3

luna.question: Which constructors had the top 3 combined points from their best driver and team, and in which years did they achieve them?
luna.sql:
WITH final_rounds AS (
    SELECT r.year, MAX(r.round) AS final_round
    FROM races AS r
    JOIN constructor_standings AS cs
      ON cs.race_id = r.race_id
    GROUP BY r.year
),
final_races AS (
    SELECT r.year, r.race_id
    FROM races AS r
    JOIN final_rounds AS fr
      ON fr.year = r.year
     AND fr.final_round = r.round
),
constructor_final_points AS (
    SELECT fr.year, cs.constructor_id, cs.points AS team_points
    FROM final_races AS fr
    JOIN constructor_standings AS cs
      ON cs.race_id = fr.race_id
),
driver_final_points AS (
    SELECT fr.year, ds.driver_id, ds.points AS driver_points
    FROM final_races AS fr
    JOIN driver_standings AS ds
      ON ds.race_id = fr.race_id
),
best_driver_points AS (
    SELECT tdr.year,
           tdr.constructor_id,
           MAX(dfp.driver_points) AS driver_points
    FROM team_driver_ranks AS tdr
    JOIN driver_final_points AS dfp
      ON dfp.year = tdr.year
     AND dfp.driver_id = tdr.driver_id
    WHERE tdr.team_driver_rank = 1
    GROUP BY tdr.year, tdr.constructor_id
)
SELECT c.name,
       bdp.year,
       bdp.driver_points + cfp.team_points AS combined_points
FROM best_driver_points AS bdp
JOIN constructor_final_points AS cfp
  ON cfp.year = bdp.year
 AND cfp.constructor_id = bdp.constructor_id
JOIN constructors AS c
  ON c.constructor_id = bdp.constructor_id
ORDER BY combined_points DESC, bdp.year DESC, c.name
LIMIT 3

luna.question: Among Formula 1 drivers who raced during the 1950s, which drivers completed a season in that decade with the same constructor in both the first and the last race they participated in, while also taking part in at least two distinct race rounds during that season?
luna.sql:
WITH driver_season_races AS (
    SELECT
        res.driver_id,
        r.year,
        r.round,
        r.race_id,
        res.constructor_id,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY res.driver_id, r.year
            ORDER BY r.round, r.race_id
        ) AS first_race,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY res.driver_id, r.year
            ORDER BY r.round DESC, r.race_id DESC
        ) AS last_race
    FROM results AS res
    JOIN races AS r ON r.race_id = res.race_id
    WHERE r.year BETWEEN 1950 AND 1959
),
qualified_seasons AS (
    SELECT driver_id, year
    FROM driver_season_races
    GROUP BY driver_id, year
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT round) >= 2
       AND MAX(CASE WHEN first_race = 1 THEN constructor_id END) =
           MAX(CASE WHEN last_race = 1 THEN constructor_id END)
)
SELECT DISTINCT d.full_name
FROM qualified_seasons AS qs
JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driver_id = qs.driver_id
ORDER BY d.full_name

luna.question: Calculate the overall average first round and average last round of races missed by Formula 1 drivers across all years. Include only drivers who missed fewer than three races in a given year and who switched teams between their appearances immediately before and after their hiatus (i.e., the constructor ID for the race right before their first missed race must be different from the constructor ID for the race right after their last missed race in that year). Do not group results by year; return just the overall averages across the entire dataset.
luna.sql:
WITH ordered_appearances AS (
    SELECT
        res.driver_id,
        r.year,
        r.round,
        res.constructor_id,
        LAG(r.round) OVER (
            PARTITION BY res.driver_id, r.year
            ORDER BY r.round
        ) AS previous_round,
        LAG(res.constructor_id) OVER (
            PARTITION BY res.driver_id, r.year
            ORDER BY r.round
        ) AS previous_constructor_id
    FROM results AS res
    JOIN races AS r
      ON r.race_id = res.race_id
),
qualifying_hiatuses AS (
    SELECT
        previous_round + 1 AS first_missed_round,
        round - 1 AS last_missed_round
    FROM ordered_appearances
    WHERE round - previous_round BETWEEN 2 AND 3
      AND previous_constructor_id <> constructor_id
)
SELECT
    AVG(first_missed_round),
    AVG(last_missed_round)
FROM qualifying_hiatuses

luna.question: Provide the full names of drivers who have been overtaken on track more times than they have overtaken others on track during race laps, excluding position changes due to pit stops (both at pit entry and exit), retirements, or position changes that occurred during the first lap of a race (considered as start movements).
luna.sql:
WITH ordered_positions AS (
    SELECT
        lp.race_id,
        lp.driver_id,
        lp.lap,
        lp.position,
        lp.lap_type,
        LAG(lp.position) OVER (
            PARTITION BY lp.race_id, lp.driver_id
            ORDER BY lp.lap
        ) AS previous_position
    FROM lap_positions AS lp
),
driver_changes AS (
    SELECT
        driver_id,
        SUM(
            CASE
                WHEN position < previous_position THEN previous_position - position
                ELSE 0
            END
        ) AS overtakes,
        SUM(
            CASE
                WHEN position > previous_position THEN position - previous_position
                ELSE 0
            END
        ) AS times_overtaken
    FROM ordered_positions
    WHERE lap > 1
      AND lower(lap_type) = 'race'
      AND position IS NOT NULL
      AND previous_position IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY driver_id
)
SELECT d.full_name
FROM driver_changes AS c
JOIN drivers AS d
  ON d.driver_id = c.driver_id

    SELECT date('2017-01-01')
    UNION ALL
    SELECT date(day, '+1 day')
    FROM calendar
    WHERE day < date('2018-08-29')
),
toy_daily AS (
    SELECT
        date(o.order_purchase_timestamp) AS day,
        SUM(oi.price) AS sales
    FROM orders AS o
    JOIN order_items AS oi
        ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
    JOIN products AS p
        ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
    JOIN product_category_name_translation AS pct
        ON pct.product_category_name = p.product_category_name
    WHERE pct.product_category_name_english = 'toys'
      AND date(o.order_purchase_timestamp) BETWEEN date('2017-01-01') AND date('2018-08-29')
    GROUP BY date(o.order_purchase_timestamp)
),
training AS (
    SELECT
        c.day,
        COALESCE(td.sales, 0.0) AS sales
    FROM calendar AS c
    LEFT JOIN toy_daily AS td
        ON td.day = c.day
),
moments AS (
    SELECT
        COUNT(*) AS n,
        SUM(julianday(day)) AS sx,
        SUM(sales) AS sy,
        SUM(julianday(day) * sales) AS sxy,
        SUM(julianday(day) * julianday(day)) AS sx2
    FROM training
),
model AS (
    SELECT
        (n * sxy - sx * sy) / (n * sx2 - sx * sx) AS slope,

    FROM moments
),

    SELECT date('2018-12-03')

    FROM prediction_days
    WHERE day < date('2018-12-10')
),
predictions AS (
    SELECT
        pd.day,
        m.intercept + m.slope * julianday(pd.day) AS predicted_sales
    FROM prediction_days AS pd
    CROSS JOIN model AS m
),
target_dates(day) AS (
    VALUES
        ('2018-12-05'),
        ('2018-12-06'),
        ('2018-12-07'),
        ('2018-12-08')
),
moving_averages AS (
    SELECT
        t.day,
        AVG(p.predicted_sales) AS moving_average
    FROM target_dates AS t
    JOIN predictions AS p
        ON p.day BETWEEN date(t.day, '-2 day') AND date(t.day, '+2 day')
    GROUP BY t.day

luna+jevtool.question: Please help me identify the top 3 bowlers who, in the overs where the maximum runs were conceded in each match, gave up the highest number of runs in a single over across all matches. For each of these bowlers, provide the match in which they conceded these maximum runs. Only consider overs that had the most runs conceded within their respective matches, and among these, determine which bowlers conceded the most runs in a single over overall.
luna+jevtool.sql:
WITH over_runs AS (
    SELECT
        b.match_id,
        b.over_id,
        b.innings_no,
        SUM(
            COALESCE(s.runs_scored, 0) +
            CASE
                WHEN e.extra_type IN ('wides', 'noballs') THEN COALESCE(e.extra_runs, 0)
                ELSE 0
            END
        ) AS runs_conceded
    FROM ball_by_ball AS b
    LEFT JOIN batsman_scored AS s
        ON s.match_id = b.match_id
       AND s.over_id = b.over_id
       AND s.ball_id = b.ball_id
       AND s.innings_no = b.innings_no
    LEFT JOIN extra_runs AS e
        ON e.match_id = b.match_id
       AND e.over_id = b.over_id
       AND e.ball_id = b.ball_id
       AND e.innings_no = b.innings_no
    GROUP BY b.match_id, b.over_id, b.innings_no
),
match_max AS (
    SELECT match_id, MAX(runs_conceded) AS max_runs
    FROM over_runs
    GROUP BY match_id
),
qualifying_overs AS (
    SELECT
        o.bowler,
        r.match_id,
        r.over_id,
        r.innings_no,
        r.runs_conceded
    FROM over_runs AS r
    JOIN match_max AS m
        ON m.match_id = r.match_id
       AND m.max_runs = r.runs_conceded
    JOIN (
        SELECT DISTINCT match_id, over_id, innings_no, bowler
        FROM ball_by_ball
    ) AS o
        ON o.match_id = r.match_id
       AND o.over_id = r.over_id
       AND o.innings_no = r.innings_no
),
bowler_best AS (
    SELECT
        q.*,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY q.bowler
            ORDER BY q.runs_conceded DESC, q.match_id, q.innings_no, q.over_id
        ) AS bowler_rank
    FROM qualifying_overs AS q
),
top_bowlers AS (
    SELECT
        b.*,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            ORDER BY b.runs_conceded DESC, b.bowler, b.match_id, b.innings_no, b.over_id
        ) AS overall_rank
    FROM bowler_best AS b
    WHERE b.bowler_rank = 1
)
SELECT
    p.player_name,
    t.match_id,
    t.runs_conceded
FROM top_bowlers AS t
JOIN player AS p
    ON p.player_id = t.bowler
WHERE t.overall_rank <= 3
ORDER BY t.overall_rank

WITH bowler_runs AS (

        SUM(COALESCE(s.runs_scored, 0) + COALESCE(e.extra_runs, 0)) AS total_runs
    FROM ball_by_ball AS b
    LEFT JOIN batsman_scored AS s
        ON s.match_id = b.match_id
       AND s.over_id = b.over_id
       AND s.ball_id = b.ball_id
       AND s.innings_no = b.innings_no
    LEFT JOIN extra_runs AS e
        ON e.match_id = b.match_id
       AND e.over_id = b.over_id
       AND e.ball_id = b.ball_id
       AND e.innings_no = b.innings_no
    GROUP BY b.bowler
),
bowler_wickets AS (
    SELECT
        b.bowler AS player_id,
        COUNT(*) AS wickets
    FROM ball_by_ball AS b
    JOIN wicket_taken AS w
        ON w.match_id = b.match_id
       AND w.over_id = b.over_id
       AND w.ball_id = b.ball_id
       AND w.innings_no = b.innings_no
    GROUP BY b.bowler
)

FROM bowler_runs AS r
JOIN bowler_wickets AS w ON w.player_id = r.player_id
JOIN player AS p ON p.player_id = r.player_id

LIMIT 1

),

    VALUES (2021), (2022), (2023)
),
monthly_totals AS (
    SELECT
        y.report_year,
        m.month_num,
        m.month_name,
        COALESCE(c.city_count, 0) AS monthly_total
    FROM years AS y
    CROSS JOIN months AS m
    LEFT JOIN (
        SELECT
            CAST(strftime('%Y', insert_date) AS INTEGER) AS report_year,
            CAST(strftime('%m', insert_date) AS INTEGER) AS month_num,
            COUNT(*) AS city_count
        FROM cities
        WHERE CAST(strftime('%Y', insert_date) AS INTEGER) BETWEEN 2021 AND 2023
          AND CAST(strftime('%m', insert_date) AS INTEGER) IN (4, 5, 6)
        GROUP BY
            CAST(strftime('%Y', insert_date) AS INTEGER),

),
running_totals AS (

        SUM(monthly_total) OVER (

            ORDER BY report_year
            ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW

    FROM monthly_totals
),
comparisons AS (
    SELECT
        report_year,
        month_num,
        month_name,
        monthly_total,

            ORDER BY report_year

    END AS monthly_growth_percentage,
    CASE
        WHEN previous_cumulative_total IS NULL OR previous_cumulative_total = 0 THEN NULL
        ELSE (cumulative_total - previous_cumulative_total) * 100.0 / previous_cumulative_total

          WHEN 2 THEN m.home_player_2
          WHEN 3 THEN m.home_player_3
          WHEN 4 THEN m.home_player_4
          WHEN 5 THEN m.home_player_5
          WHEN 6 THEN m.home_player_6
          WHEN 7 THEN m.home_player_7
          WHEN 8 THEN m.home_player_8
          WHEN 9 THEN m.home_player_9
          WHEN 10 THEN m.home_player_10
          WHEN 11 THEN m.home_player_11
        END
        ELSE CASE s.n
          WHEN 1 THEN m.away_player_1
          WHEN 2 THEN m.away_player_2
          WHEN 3 THEN m.away_player_3
          WHEN 4 THEN m.away_player_4
          WHEN 5 THEN m.away_player_5
          WHEN 6 THEN m.away_player_6
          WHEN 7 THEN m.away_player_7
          WHEN 8 THEN m.away_player_8
          WHEN 9 THEN m.away_player_9
          WHEN 10 THEN m.away_player_10
          WHEN 11 THEN m.away_player_11
        END

      m.home_team_goal,
      m.away_team_goal
    FROM "Match" AS m
    CROSS JOIN slots AS s
    CROSS JOIN sides AS d
  ),
  participation AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
      match_id,
      player_api_id,
      CASE

    GROUP BY p.player_api_id, p.player_name, x.outcome
  ),

    FROM counts AS c

luna+jevtool.sql:
WITH ball_pairs AS (
    SELECT
        b.match_id,
        b.innings_no,
        b.striker,
        CASE
            WHEN b.striker < b.non_striker THEN b.striker
            ELSE b.non_striker
        END AS player_a,
        CASE
            WHEN b.striker < b.non_striker THEN b.non_striker
            ELSE b.striker
        END AS player_b,
        COALESCE(s.runs_scored, 0) AS runs_scored
    FROM ball_by_ball AS b
    LEFT JOIN batsman_scored AS s
        ON s.match_id = b.match_id
       AND s.over_id = b.over_id
       AND s.ball_id = b.ball_id
       AND s.innings_no = b.innings_no
),
partnerships AS (
    SELECT
        match_id,
        innings_no,
        player_a,
        player_b,
        SUM(CASE WHEN striker = player_a THEN runs_scored ELSE 0 END) AS score_a,
        SUM(CASE WHEN striker = player_b THEN runs_scored ELSE 0 END) AS score_b
    FROM ball_pairs
    GROUP BY match_id, innings_no, player_a, player_b
),
ordered_partnerships AS (
    SELECT
        match_id,
        CASE
            WHEN score_a > score_b
              OR (score_a = score_b AND player_a > player_b)
            THEN player_a
            ELSE player_b
        END AS player1_id,
        CASE
            WHEN score_a > score_b
              OR (score_a = score_b AND player_a > player_b)
            THEN score_a
            ELSE score_b
        END AS player1_score,
        CASE
            WHEN score_a > score_b
              OR (score_a = score_b AND player_a > player_b)
            THEN player_b
            ELSE player_a
        END AS player2_id,
        CASE
            WHEN score_a > score_b
              OR (score_a = score_b AND player_a > player_b)
            THEN score_b
            ELSE score_a
        END AS player2_score,
        score_a + score_b AS partnership_score
    FROM partnerships
),
ranked_partnerships AS (
    SELECT
        ordered_partnerships.*,
        RANK() OVER (
            PARTITION BY match_id
            ORDER BY partnership_score DESC
        ) AS partnership_rank
    FROM ordered_partnerships
)
SELECT
    match_id,
    player1_id,
    player1_score,
    player2_id,
    player2_score,
    partnership_score
FROM ranked_partnerships
WHERE partnership_rank = 1
ORDER BY match_id, player1_id, player2_id

    LEFT JOIN batsman_scored AS bs

       AND er.ball_id = b.ball_id

            b2.bowler,
            b2.match_id,
            COUNT(*) AS wickets

luna+jevtool.question: What is the average forecasted annual sales for products 4160 and 7790 during 2018, using monthly sales data starting from January 2016 for the first 36 months, applying seasonality adjustments from time steps 7 through 30, and employing a weighted regression method to estimate sales?
luna+jevtool.sql:
WITH
initial AS (
    SELECT
        product_id,
        mth,
        qty,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY product_id
            ORDER BY mth
        ) AS rn
    FROM monthly_sales
    WHERE product_id IN (4160, 7790)
      AND mth >= '2016-01-01'
),
sales AS (
    SELECT product_id, mth, qty, rn
    FROM initial
    WHERE rn <= 36
),
moving AS (
    SELECT
        product_id,
        mth,
        qty,
        rn,
        AVG(qty) OVER (
            PARTITION BY product_id
            ORDER BY rn
            ROWS BETWEEN 5 PRECEDING AND 6 FOLLOWING
        ) AS ma_5_6,
        AVG(qty) OVER (
            PARTITION BY product_id
            ORDER BY rn
            ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND 5 FOLLOWING
        ) AS ma_6_5
    FROM sales
),
cma_rows AS (
    SELECT
        product_id,
        mth,
        qty,
        rn,
        (ma_5_6 + ma_6_5) / 2.0 AS cma
    FROM moving
    WHERE rn BETWEEN 7 AND 30
),
seasonal_indices AS (
    SELECT
        product_id,
        strftime('%m', mth) AS month_no,
        AVG(qty / NULLIF(cma, 0.0)) AS seasonality
    FROM cma_rows
    GROUP BY product_id, strftime('%m', mth)
),
adjusted AS (
    SELECT
        s.product_id,
        s.rn,
        s.qty / NULLIF(si.seasonality, 0.0) AS adjusted_qty
    FROM sales AS s
    JOIN seasonal_indices AS si
      ON si.product_id = s.product_id
     AND si.month_no = strftime('%m', s.mth)
    WHERE s.rn BETWEEN 7 AND 30
),
regression_stats AS (
    SELECT
        product_id,
        SUM(1.0 * rn) AS sw,
        SUM(1.0 * rn * rn) AS swx,
        SUM(1.0 * rn * rn * rn) AS swxx,
        SUM(1.0 * rn * adjusted_qty) AS swy,
        SUM(1.0 * rn * rn * adjusted_qty) AS swxy
    FROM adjusted
    GROUP BY product_id
),
regression AS (
    SELECT
        product_id,
        (sw * swxy - swx * swy) /
            NULLIF(sw * swxx - swx * swx, 0.0) AS slope,
        swy,
        swx,
        sw
    FROM regression_stats
),
coefficients AS (
    SELECT
        product_id,
        slope,
        (swy - slope * swx) / NULLIF(sw, 0.0) AS intercept
    FROM regression
),
forecast_months AS (
    SELECT
        s.product_id,
        s.rn,
        si.seasonality
    FROM sales AS s
    JOIN seasonal_indices AS si
      ON si.product_id = s.product_id
     AND si.month_no = strftime('%m', s.mth)
    WHERE s.rn BETWEEN 25 AND 36
      AND strftime('%Y', s.mth) = '2018'
),
annual_forecasts AS (
    SELECT
        f.product_id,
        SUM((c.intercept + c.slope * f.rn) * f.seasonality) AS annual_forecast
    FROM forecast_months AS f
    JOIN coefficients AS c
      ON c.product_id = f.product_id
    GROUP BY f.product_id
)

FROM annual_forecasts

WITH eligible_races AS (
    SELECT race_id
    FROM races_ext
    WHERE is_pit_data_available = 1
),
typical_pit AS (
    SELECT AVG(ps.milliseconds) AS avg_milliseconds
    FROM pit_stops AS ps
    JOIN eligible_races AS er
      ON er.race_id = ps.race_id
    WHERE ps.milliseconds IS NOT NULL
),
classified AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        x.race_id,
        x.lap,
        x.driver_id AS overtaken_driver_id,
        y.driver_id AS overtaking_driver_id,
        CASE
            WHEN EXISTS (
                SELECT 1
                FROM retirements AS r
                WHERE r.race_id = x.race_id
                  AND r.driver_id = x.driver_id
                  AND r.lap = x.lap
            ) THEN 'R'
            WHEN EXISTS (
                SELECT 1
                FROM pit_stops AS ps
                WHERE ps.race_id = x.race_id
                  AND ps.driver_id = x.driver_id
                  AND ps.lap = x.lap
            )
            OR (
                EXISTS (
                    SELECT 1
                    FROM pit_stops AS ps
                    WHERE ps.race_id = x.race_id
                      AND ps.driver_id = x.driver_id
                      AND ps.lap = x.lap - 1
                )
                AND tx.running_milliseconds IS NOT NULL
                AND ty.running_milliseconds IS NOT NULL
                AND ABS(tx.running_milliseconds - ty.running_milliseconds) < tp.avg_milliseconds
            ) THEN 'P'
            WHEN x.lap = 1
                 AND ABS(gx.grid - gy.grid) <= 2 THEN 'S'
            ELSE 'T'
        END AS overtake_type
    FROM lap_positions AS x
    JOIN lap_positions AS y
      ON y.race_id = x.race_id
     AND y.lap = x.lap
     AND y.driver_id <> x.driver_id
    JOIN eligible_races AS er
      ON er.race_id = x.race_id
    LEFT JOIN lap_positions AS px
      ON px.race_id = x.race_id
     AND px.driver_id = x.driver_id
     AND px.lap = x.lap - 1
    LEFT JOIN lap_positions AS py
      ON py.race_id = y.race_id
     AND py.driver_id = y.driver_id
     AND py.lap = y.lap - 1
    LEFT JOIN results AS gx
      ON gx.race_id = x.race_id
     AND gx.driver_id = x.driver_id
    LEFT JOIN results AS gy
      ON gy.race_id = y.race_id
     AND gy.driver_id = y.driver_id
    LEFT JOIN lap_times_ext AS tx
      ON tx.race_id = x.race_id
     AND tx.driver_id = x.driver_id
     AND tx.lap = x.lap
    LEFT JOIN lap_times_ext AS ty
      ON ty.race_id = y.race_id
     AND ty.driver_id = y.driver_id
     AND ty.lap = y.lap
    CROSS JOIN typical_pit AS tp
    WHERE x.position > y.position
      AND (
            (
                x.lap = 1
                AND gx.grid > 0
                AND gy.grid > 0
                AND gx.grid < gy.grid
            )
            OR (
                x.lap > 1
                AND px.position <= py.position
            )
          )
),
labels(label) AS (
    VALUES ('R'), ('P'), ('S'), ('T')
)

    COUNT(classified.overtake_type) AS overtake_count
FROM labels
LEFT JOIN classified
  ON classified.overtake_type = labels.label
GROUP BY labels.label
ORDER BY CASE labels.label

WITH ordered AS (
    SELECT
        lp.race_id,
        lp.driver_id,
        lp.lap,
        lp.position,
        lp.lap_type,
        LAG(lp.lap) OVER (
            PARTITION BY lp.race_id, lp.driver_id
            ORDER BY lp.lap
        ) AS previous_lap,
        LAG(lp.position) OVER (
            PARTITION BY lp.race_id, lp.driver_id
            ORDER BY lp.lap
        ) AS previous_position
    FROM lap_positions AS lp
),
valid AS (
    SELECT o.*
    FROM ordered AS o
    WHERE o.lap > 1
      AND o.previous_lap = o.lap - 1
      AND o.position IS NOT NULL
      AND o.previous_position IS NOT NULL
      AND lower(COALESCE(o.lap_type, '')) NOT LIKE '%start%'
      AND lower(COALESCE(o.lap_type, '')) NOT LIKE '%pit%'
      AND lower(COALESCE(o.lap_type, '')) NOT LIKE '%retir%'
      AND NOT EXISTS (
          SELECT 1
          FROM pit_stops AS ps
          WHERE ps.race_id = o.race_id
            AND ps.driver_id = o.driver_id
            AND ps.lap IN (o.lap, o.lap - 1)
      )
      AND NOT EXISTS (
          SELECT 1
          FROM retirements AS rt
          WHERE rt.race_id = o.race_id
            AND rt.driver_id = o.driver_id
            AND rt.lap IN (o.lap, o.lap - 1)
      )
),
events AS (
    SELECT
        CASE
            WHEN a.previous_position > b.previous_position
             AND a.position < b.position
            THEN a.driver_id
            ELSE b.driver_id
        END AS overtaker_id,
        CASE
            WHEN a.previous_position > b.previous_position
             AND a.position < b.position
            THEN b.driver_id
            ELSE a.driver_id
        END AS overtaken_id
    FROM valid AS a
    JOIN valid AS b
      ON b.race_id = a.race_id
     AND b.lap = a.lap
     AND b.driver_id > a.driver_id
    WHERE (
              a.previous_position > b.previous_position
          AND a.position < b.position
          )
       OR (
              a.previous_position < b.previous_position
          AND a.position > b.position
          )
),
counts AS (
    SELECT
        driver_id,
        SUM(overtakes) AS overtakes,
        SUM(overtaken) AS overtaken
    FROM (
        SELECT overtaker_id AS driver_id, 1 AS overtakes, 0 AS overtaken
        FROM events
        UNION ALL
        SELECT overtaken_id AS driver_id, 0 AS overtakes, 1 AS overtaken
        FROM events
    ) AS e
    GROUP BY driver_id
)

FROM counts AS c
JOIN drivers AS d
  ON d.driver_id = c.driver_id
WHERE c.overtaken > c.overtakes
ORDER BY d.full_name
